death_sites.place: Elukwatini / Badplaas area, infant swept from mother's arms crossing flooded river
death_sites.census_place_name: Lukwatini (Elukwatini). Badplaas town main place for comparison: SiSwati 40.04, Afrikaans 31.71, English 12.80 (pop 582) - https://census2011.adrianfrith.com/place/860005
death_sites.count_note: TimesLIVE: 'flooded river in Badplaas'; Wikipedia: 'A mother and baby were swept away while crossing a flooded river in Elukwatini, and a one year old drowned' - likely same incident.

death_sites.place: Outside Pilgrim's Rest / Blyde River, adult man drowned crossing river
death_sites.census_place_name: Pilgrim's Rest (Thaba Chweu LM: Sepedi 36.17, SiSwati 17.84, Afrikaans 15.25)
death_sites.count_note: Wikipedia: 'body of a 35-year-old man who had drowned in the Blyde River' - Blyde rises near Pilgrim's Rest; probably the same death.

dominant_language_across_sites: SiSwati (Mpumalanga sites); isiZulu at the KZN site; Sepedi at Pilgrim's Rest
notes: Only 4 of the >=10 SA deaths could be tied to places (each 1 death, so counts are per-incident). Mpumalanga's 10 confirmed deaths (4 Feb) were not broken down by place in FloodList. Tshakhuma (Vhembe, Limpopo) and Mkhuhlu (Bushbuckridge) were the most-damaged areas but no deaths found there. Sources quoted SAWS safety advice in English ('Do not cross rivers without first checking water levels') but nothing on warning language.
